evidence.product_understanding: analysis.md §1 separates given facts, seven numbered assumptions (for example that outstanding invitations count toward the Starter limit) and open questions; §5 and §7 keep activation risks and unresolved policy questions explicit. It invents no pricing, upgrade, integration or analytics behavior.
evidence.ux_reasoning: analysis.md §2 gives an explicit journey (create project -> optional invite -> done; Save & exit -> paused workspace -> resume) and §3 justifies project-first sequencing and deferred workspace/plan questions. app.js handleProjectSubmit creates the project before entering 'invite', and primaryButton() offers 'Continue without inviting' when the list is empty, so the project is secured before any invitation decision.
evidence.design_judgment: The role guide is placed above the selectors (analysis.md §3; app.js roleCardsHTML/inviteScreen), invitations are capped at four with 'Starter limit reached' and no upgrade path (seatMeterHTML), and the done screen makes Open project primary. Weaker choices: the optional description is permanently expanded, and a three-step rail plus workspace card give a one-field task more chrome than necessary.
evidence.visual_hierarchy: screenshots/desktop.png (1280x988) has one dominant serif H1, a short lede, two clearly labeled fields and a single deep-green CTA inside one panel; mobile.png (390x1096) stacks the same order. test-output/checks.json confirms document_width = client_width (1280 and 390, no horizontal overflow). The floating Prototype controls pill overlaps the 'Next' note on mobile.
evidence.interaction_completeness: analysis.md §4 and app.js implement empty workspace, name validation with focus return, a creating spinner with aria-busy, success, per-row invalid/duplicate/seat-cap validation, partial invitation failure with Retry, Save & exit, localStorage reload persistence, resume, and Owner/Admin/Member gating. Project-creation failure is not simulated, although the brief only explicitly demands invitation failure.
evidence.accessibility_responsiveness: test-output/checks.json reports axe violations 0, 30 passes, controls_without_accessible_name 0, h1_count 1, has_main true, and horizontal_overflow false at both 1280 and 390. Source adds a skip link, heading/error focus management, aria-live announcements, aria-busy, labeled inputs and reduced-motion handling (styles.css line 2002).
evidence.implementation_quality: app.js is a structured IIFE with escapeHtml, normalized loadState, asyncEpoch guards against stale async work, delegated events, explicit guards while busy and localStorage persistence; styles.css uses design tokens and defined 1040/980/680/430px breakpoints. Evidence is limited to checks.json rather than a test log.

critical_defects: None blocking the solo or invitation paths. Minor: no project-creation failure state is demonstrated, and the mobile Prototype controls overlay covers body copy in screenshots/mobile.png.
strengths: Project is created before roles or invitations, and the solo path is explicit ('Continue without inviting', 'Not now', and a solo success message).
Role capabilities appear as three compact cards before the role selector; the Starter limit is visible and enforced without inventing pricing or upgrades.
Complete invitation recovery model: per-row validation, sending state, sent/failed rows, retry, continue-without-inviting and saved unsent drafts.
Clean rendered hierarchy and clean automated accessibility summary (0 unnamed controls, one h1, no overflow).
missing_evidence: analysis.md §8 says verification is recorded in transcript.md, but no transcript.md is present in the packet; checks.json covers only the initial rendered/accessibility state.
Only the create screen is captured at both viewports; the invite, role, error, success and resume screens have no rendered screenshots.

evidence.product_understanding: analysis.md §1 separates nine supplied facts, seven explicit assumptions and eight unknowns, including the load-bearing assumptions that the Owner consumes a Starter seat and that pending invitations reserve seats. §8 states activation risks and open questions; no email delivery, analytics, integration or upgrade behavior is claimed as real.
evidence.ux_reasoning: analysis.md §3 makes the project name the only required input and §4.1 sequences name -> create -> success -> Open project, placing invitations in a separate optional branch after the project exists. §4.2 defers workspace name, team size and use case, and §4.5 explains the seat-limit decision. app.js makes Open project the success screen's primary action.
evidence.design_judgment: index.html collapses the optional description behind a details element (lines 83-92), keeps one primary action on the success card, and shows '5 members in total, including you' with Team as a footnote rather than an upgrade CTA. The mobile decision to place the full role guide after the invitation form weakens 'explain capabilities before assigning roles'.
evidence.visual_hierarchy: screenshots/desktop.png (1280x921) has a clear H1 and form-first hierarchy, but the form card and 'Your workspace at a glance' card carry similar weight and a large lower area is unused. screenshots/mobile.png (390x1380) is much taller and the fixed Prototype controls bar covers the 'Your workspace at a glance' heading. checks.json reports no horizontal overflow at either viewport.
evidence.interaction_completeness: analysis.md §5 and app.js cover empty, name validation, create loading, create failure with retained values, confirmation, per-row invitation validation, partial failure with Try again, seat limit, skip on both steps, resume card, reload persistence, project shell and eight demo states. The supplied checks.json verifies rendering/accessibility only, not these interaction paths.
evidence.accessibility_responsiveness: test-output/checks.json reports axe violations 0 and no overflow, but h1_count = 5 and controls_without_accessible_name = 2 of 40 at both viewports. Source uses native controls, fieldset legends, progressbars and box-shadow focus rings (styles.css lines 639-644); the unnamed controls and duplicate page-level h1s need correction.
evidence.implementation_quality: app.js uses consistent escaping for injected HTML, guarded state transitions, dynamic invite fieldsets/legends and localStorage persistence. The static multi-view document leaves five h1s in the DOM and two controls unnamed, and the claimed 41-check suite is not supplied, so generated-markup QA is weaker than candidate A's.

critical_defects: Non-blocking requirement gap: below 720px the complete 'What each role can do' guide renders after the invitation form (index.html 207-289; styles.css @media 720), so the full capability explanation is not before the first role selection, although a summary line and per-select help are present.
Accessibility defect to verify and fix: test-output/checks.json reports 2 of 40 controls without an accessible name and 5 h1 elements in the document.
strengths: Shortest credible activation path: one required field, project creation, then Open project as the primary success action.
Invitations are clearly a post-activation, optional branch, with skip on both steps and a contextual resume card rather than a checklist.
Seat and role copy is explicit that the Owner is included and that pending rows reserve seats; no pricing or upgrade flow is fabricated.
State model includes project-creation failure as well as partial invitation failure and retry, exceeding the brief's explicit failure-state requirement.
missing_evidence: analysis.md §10 claims 41 automated checks passed, but the packet contains only test-output/checks.json, which holds desktop/mobile render and axe summaries, not the claimed 41-check log.
Only the create screen is captured at both viewports; success, invite, error, project-shell and resume screens have no rendered screenshots.

comparison: Candidate A is the stronger delivered artifact overall (3.85 vs 3.50 weighted). Candidate A has the more authoritative rendered hierarchy, a cleaner accessibility result (0 unnamed controls and one h1, versus 2 unnamed of 40 and five h1s for Candidate B) and more defensive implementation structure. Candidate B has the better activation design: name -> create -> Open project, with invitations moved into a clearly optional post-success branch, whereas Candidate A interposes a full optional invitation screen before its completion screen and requires an extra acknowledgement to reach Open project. Candidate B also models project-creation failure, which Candidate A does not, but Candidate B's mobile role-guide order and generated-markup accessibility issues cost it in the rubric.
limitations: This is one blinded judge pass, not a statistical test and not proof of causation. Only the create screen is rendered in each packet (desktop 1280x988/921, mobile 390x1096/1380); I inspected those screenshots directly but did not execute the prototypes, so interaction completeness is judged against source code and supplied checks rather than live runs, and no manual screen-reader or cross-browser test was performed. Both packets omit the end-to-end verification logs their analyses claim. The packet manifests contain candidate metadata fields that conflict with the immutable packet labels assigned in instructions.md and judge-prompt.md; I ignored those fields, did not read mapping.json or other passes, and scored only the evidence inside inputs/.
